senses.gloss: One complete turn of something around a center point.
examples: The engine runs at three thousand *revolutions* per minute.
Each *revolution* of the crank pulls the bucket up a foot.
The Earth makes one *revolution* around the sun each year.

senses.gloss: A complete and far-reaching change in the way people live or do things.
examples: The digital *revolution* changed how we shop and read.
Antibiotics brought about a *revolution* in medicine.
She calls the new battery a *revolution* in clean energy.

senses.gloss: Something that stops progress on a plan or project.
examples: Funding turned out to be the biggest *roadblock*.
We hit a *roadblock* when the supplier backed out.
Their lawyers threw up one *roadblock* after another.

senses.gloss: An animal or object killed or offered to a god in a religious ceremony.
examples: The priests performed a *sacrifice* at dawn.
A lamb was offered as a *sacrifice* for a good harvest.
The museum explains how such *sacrifices* were carried out.

senses.gloss: A person or thing that saves someone from trouble or ruin.
examples: That loan was the *salvation* of the family farm.
Coaching kids became his *salvation* after the divorce.
Air conditioning is my *salvation* in August.

senses.gloss: The use of a short piece of an existing recording inside a new song.
examples: The album leans heavily on *sampling* of old funk records.
*Sampling* without permission can end in a lawsuit.
He built the whole track out of *sampling* and a drum machine.

senses.gloss: A raised wooden platform on which a prisoner is hanged.
examples: The condemned man was led to the *scaffold* at dawn.
A crowd gathered around the *scaffold* in the town square.
He went to the *scaffold* still insisting he was innocent.

senses.gloss: Serious academic study and the deep knowledge that comes from it.
examples: Her book is a fine piece of *scholarship*.
Recent *scholarship* has questioned that date.
The prize honors a lifetime of *scholarship* on the Civil War.

senses.gloss: A breakfast dish of eggs stirred as they cook, usually with other things mixed in.
examples: I ordered the veggie *scramble* with wheat toast.
She makes a tofu *scramble* every Sunday morning.
Their *scramble* comes with bacon, peppers, and cheese.

senses.gloss: The testing or checking of many people to catch a disease or to filter out anyone unsuitable.
examples: The clinic offers free *screening* for high blood pressure.
*Screening* at the airport took almost an hour.
Every volunteer goes through a background *screening*.

senses.gloss: A mixed drink of vodka and orange juice.
examples: He ordered a *screwdriver* at the hotel bar.
Brunch comes with a free mimosa or *screwdriver*.
She makes *screwdrivers* with fresh-squeezed juice.

senses.gloss: In football, the play that begins when the ball is snapped, or the line where the two teams face off.
examples: The quarterback read the defense at the line of *scrimmage*.
He gained ninety yards from *scrimmage* on Sunday.
A false start moved the line of *scrimmage* back five yards.

senses.gloss: A wide view of the sea and the coast.
examples: The porch looks out on a stunning *seascape*.
Fog rolled in and swallowed the whole *seascape*.
We watched the *seascape* change color as the sun went down.

senses.gloss: The head of a major department of the United States government.
examples: The *secretary* of defense testified before the committee.
He served as *secretary* of the treasury for four years.
Two cabinet *secretaries* resigned in the same week.

senses.gloss: The act of choosing someone or something, or the one that is chosen.
examples: The *selection* of a new principal took months.
His *selection* for the national team surprised no one.
The judges announced their *selections* on Friday.

senses.gloss: A tendency of the body to react badly to a food, a drug, or something such as light or cold.
senses.ru: повышенная чувствительность (к пище, свету и т. п.)
examples: She has a *sensitivity* to dairy but not a true allergy.
The whitening strips gave me tooth *sensitivity* for a week.
*Sensitivity* to light is a common migraine symptom.

senses.gloss: Care and understanding in dealing with other people's feelings.
examples: He handled the layoffs with real *sensitivity*.
The reporter wrote about the family with unusual *sensitivity*.
Her manager could use a little more *sensitivity*.

senses.gloss: A group of words that expresses a complete thought.
examples: Write your answer in one complete *sentence*.
That *sentence* is missing a verb.
He reads the first two *sentences* of an article and stops.

senses.gloss: A section of a movie showing one continuous piece of action.
examples: The opening *sequence* was shot in a single take.
That chase *sequence* runs almost ten minutes.
They cut the dream *sequence* from the final version.
